subject: literature
passage: When Emily Dickinson's poems were first published in 1890, four years after her death, the editors made many changes. Among other things, they replaced most of her frequent dashes with commas, periods, and semicolons. The editors believed these changes made the unusual poems easier for readers to follow, and the volume sold well.
passage_b: Readers of the 1955 edition, which restored the punctuation of Dickinson's manuscripts, met a different poet. Her dashes, many scholars argue, are not careless marks but part of the poems' meaning: they create pauses, leave thoughts open, and let a line point in more than one direction at once. Replacing them with ordinary punctuation made the poems tidier, but it also narrowed them.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the editors' changes in Text 1?

choices.A: By arguing that the 1890 volume failed because readers found the poems confusing
choices.B: By agreeing that the changes brought the poems closer to Dickinson's intentions
choices.C: By claiming that Dickinson's manuscripts contained very few dashes
choices.D: By suggesting that the changes made the poems neater but lost some of their meaning

explanation.why: Text 1 says the editors replaced Dickinson's dashes to make the poems "easier for readers to follow." Text 2 says the dashes are "part of the poems' meaning" and that replacing them "made the poems tidier, but it also narrowed them." So Text 2 grants a gain in neatness but sees a loss in meaning.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 1 says the volume "sold well," and Text 2 never claims it failed.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says the dashes are part of the poems' meaning, so removing them moved the poems away from what Dickinson wrote.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 says the 1955 edition restored the punctuation of the manuscripts, including the dashes, so the manuscripts had many.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2 calls the edited poems "tidier" but "narrowed," meaning they lost some of their range of meaning.
